name: Neetu Yoshi Limited

GOV.explanation: IPO cost and utilization discrepancies remain material. Related financial allocations and concentrated management control warrant close scrutiny.
GOV.counterevidence: Unmodified audit and IFC opinions, matching bank returns, no reported default or fraud, and promoter warrant participation oppose a severe-abuse conclusion.

MOAT.explanation: RDSO safety-item qualifications, integrated casting and machining, and repeat orders form useful but contestable barriers.
MOAT.counterevidence: Concentrated buyers, tender price pressure and established approved competitors constrain pricing power.

REV.explanation: The selected manufacturing-comparable FY2024–26 standalone CAGR is 44.23%. A starting 9 is capped at 8 for short comparable history and Medium confidence.
REV.counterevidence: Five- and three-year organic manufacturing histories are not comparable across the trading transition. A price-versus-volume bridge is unavailable.

DUR.explanation: New capacity and dated orders provide access beyond legacy components. Fleet maintenance and replacement support repeat demand.
DUR.counterevidence: Government and OEM concentration, qualification timing and an unreconciled order book limit duration confidence.

CAP.explanation: Incremental NOPAT/IC is mixed: 22.11%, then 8.23%, and 11.42% across FY2024–26. The reference capital cost is 12–16%; substantial CWIP has not matured.
CAP.counterevidence: The earlier cohort exceeded the upper capital-cost reference. The recent low return may reflect timing rather than permanently poor economics.

CASH.explanation: Three-year reported CFO/PAT is 44.80%, or 47.05% after explicit economic reclasses. Receivable days rose to 118 from 54.
CASH.counterevidence: Most receivables are less than six months overdue, and no major impairment is disclosed. Original and comparative cash-flow classifications reconcile.

BAL.explanation: Debt is modest, but accessible cash after IPO earmarks is uncertain. Optional warrant consideration is not current liquidity.
BAL.counterevidence: Term loans were repaid; operating interest cover is about 18.4 times. Large equity funding and no reported default reduce traditional leverage risk. Published FY2025 working-capital sanction of ₹8 crore suggests conditional headroom of ₹4.138 crore if current access continues; this alternative is explicitly modeled.

EXEC.explanation: Manufacturing sales roughly doubled in FY2024–26 and dated orders demonstrate access. The new-plant location and schedule changed, while actual qualified output is not verified.
EXEC.counterevidence: Existing capacity expanded and approvals broadened. A changed schedule is not proof of project failure, but the record is too short for an exceptional score.

EARN.explanation: Operating EBIT rose from ₹21.70 crore to ₹28.46 crore, approximately 31.2%. Most profit remains operating after excluding interest and unrealized gold gains.
EARN.counterevidence: Operating margins declined. Other income and IPO/warrant dilution weaken the interpretation of headline earnings and weighted EPS.

R.explanation: NS: current funding and the pre-entry cash bridge are unresolved. Counterfactual rescue returns are not supported prospective equity returns.
R.counterevidence: A dated secondary reference price and full scenarios are available, but price evidence does not cure funding uncertainty.

D.explanation: NS: recovery and financeability depend on uncertain available cash, successful ramp-up and hypothetical recapitalization.
D.counterevidence: Modest debt and operating profits are genuine buffers. A modeled reserve breach is not an observed default.

P.explanation: NS: price-implied expectations can be illustrated at ₹233.40, but the reverse case requires hypothetical historical capital and unsupported line utilization at higher hurdles.
P.counterevidence: Finite mathematical roots and a dated historical quote support diagnostics, not an actionable entry range.

L.explanation: NS: the required 60-session exchange history, current restrictions and spreads are unverified. The 20-session estimate is diagnostic only.
L.counterevidence: The official 800-share lot and 20 actual dated observations establish some activity, not guaranteed exit capacity.

gates.subject: Integrity and minority protection
gates.reason: No established fraud or default. Concentrated control, related financial allocations and IPO reconciliation require stronger stewardship evidence.

gates.subject: Financial reliability
gates.reason: Bounded current IPO and liquidity reliability Hold: ₹1.3672 crore expense gap and ₹3.0065 crore utilization decrease remain unresolved. FY2025 cash-flow reclasses reconcile and are not the basis for Hold.

gates.subject: Funding and survival
gates.reason: Unreconciled earmarks and deposit availability prevent assurance of current freely available funding. Issuer-reported initial warrant receipt is now document-supported via a mirror, but the current roll-forward is not. A modeled reserve gap is not observed default. A historical ₹8 crore bank sanction provides potential ₹4.138 crore headroom; current drawing power and renewal are unverified, not assumed absent.

gates.reason: An 800-share lot and 20 dated secondary sessions are available. The required 60-session exchange history, current restrictions and spreads are unverified.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Neetu Yoshi is a railway-component casting and machining manufacturer expanding into larger assemblies. It is an industrial growth candidate, not yet a demonstrated compounder. Safety-item qualifications, repeat orders and rapidly growing sales are its strengths. Cash realization and the reconciliation of IPO-funded expansion are its principal weaknesses. FY2026 revenue rose 39.32% to ₹98.35 crore, but reported operating cash was only ₹4.03 crore against ₹25.01 crore PAT.

At the dated secondary-market reference of ₹233.40 on 19 October 2026, market capitalization is ₹905.89 crore. That is 36.21 times FY2026 profit using current issued shares and about 29.71 times operating EBITDA before unverified cash deductions. The price therefore requires substantial successful growth. Provisional BQS is 5.3/10; GQS is 5.0/10 after its persistent-cash ceiling; IAS is NS. Quality and growth diagnostics are excluded from rankings while G2 is on Hold.

Research verdict: Hold. The current IPO ledger contains material unresolved differences, although the audited cash-flow reclassifications themselves reconcile. Ordinary investment returns and an actionable buying range are not supported. A signed IPO and available-cash reconciliation, verified new-plant dispatches, and sustained collections would improve the case. A lower quote alone would not cure the funding evidence gap.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Identity: Neetu Yoshi Limited, formerly Neetu Yoshi Private Limited; ISIN INE0UZO01024; BSE SME scrip 544434; symbol NEETUYOSHI. It was incorporated on 20 January 2020 and listed on 4 July 2025. The filing CIN, U35999UR2020PLC010670, is preserved as stated. Official interoperability metadata confirms 38,812,600 issued shares and an 800-share lot. The interoperable symbol NEETUYOSH$ is not evidence of an NSE listing.

Research cutoff is 20 October 2026. Sources were retrieved on 22 October, excluding later price rows. Financial anchor: audited FY2026 consolidated IndAS accounts, cross-checked against standalone manufacturing and the small 60%-owned Neetus Delight subsidiary. Its FY2026 revenue of ₹0.1096 crore is immaterial to industrial economics. The model enters on 20 October 2026 at the preceding dated close of ₹233.40 and ends on 20 October 2031, 1,826 days later, using ACT/365.25. The nominal pre-tax equity hurdle is 15%, with 12% and 18% sensitivities. ₹500,000 is an illustrative position, not a statement of the user's holdings.

G1 is Conditional; G2, G3 and G4 are Hold. Confidence is High on audited entries, issued shares and lot size; Medium on underlying growth, incremental capital returns and analytical cash reclasses; Low on current freely available cash, actual ramp output and full-window execution capacity. Unknowns remain NS rather than an imputed neutral score.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Primitive judgments: GOV 4, MOAT 6, REV 8, DUR 7, CAP 5, CASH 3, BAL 4, EXEC 5 and EARN 6. R, D, P and L remain NS. Each factor's evidence and counterevidence are set out below. BQS is exactly 5.28, displayed 5.3. GQS is exactly 6.55 before the persistent-cash ceiling and 5.0 afterward. IAS has only 25% scored weight, a known contribution of 1.32 and a mathematical missing-factor bound of 2.07–8.82. This is not a confidence interval or a rankable point.

The embedded audit preserves exact framework weights and weighted contributions. Display uses decimal HALF_UP rounding; IAS uses unrounded BQS. Moving GOV and CAP together by one point changes BQS by ±0.32, giving 4.96–5.60. CAP alone changes raw GQS by ±0.15, but the cash ceiling still binds. CAP 5 recognizes mixed historical incremental returns and a large unfinished-capital cohort. CASH 3 reflects persistent weak realization, not simply one year of growth capex.

The G2 Hold excludes quality and growth rankings even though those factor sets are complete. High sales growth does not override funding reliability, and return or downside points are not guessed from a hypothetical recapitalization.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company purchases ferrous materials and scrap, melts and casts specified grades, performs heat treatment and machining, and sells inspected components for railway bogies, locomotives and tracks. Products include mild steel, spheroidal graphite iron, cast iron and manganese steel. Qualification, yield, rejection control, energy costs, material costs and timely delivery determine profitability. Railways and wagon or coach OEMs control inspection and acceptance; an invoice is not cash until the customer pays.

The business started as a trader in 2020, added machining in 2022 and moved to manufacturing in 2023. FY2026 consolidated revenue was ₹98.35 crore versus standalone ₹98.24 crore, overwhelmingly domestic. The food subsidiary is not a material diversification engine. The presentation classifies ₹74.18 crore as railway sales and ₹24.06 crore as private sales, but private OEMs can still serve railway end markets. This should not be described as 24% independent demand diversification.

FY2026 materials, purchases and inventory changes together were approximately ₹49.15 crore, employee costs ₹5.72 crore and other expenses ₹12.85 crore. Operating EBITDA was ₹30.63 crore after excluding other income. Three customers generated 52.35% of sales; the largest generated 28.90%. Sales access, installed capacity, qualified production and collection are four distinct milestones.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The moat mechanism combines item-specific railway safety qualification, metallurgical know-how, integrated casting and machining, and a delivery record with customers. Requalification imposes time and quality risk on buyers. More than 25 approved components and repeat orders support a useful barrier. They do not prove monopoly pricing, sole-source status or high returns on the next factory.

Competition includes Texmaco's integrated rolling-stock and foundry operations; Hindusthan Engineering's bogies, side frames, bolsters, couplers and draft gears; Steelcast's alloy-casting operations across several industrial OEM sectors; and government-owned Braithwaite's approved bogies and railway components. These primary product records support a structural comparison, not a peer valuation average. No reliable item-level denominator establishes Neetu Yoshi's market share. Promotional descriptions such as leading or unique are not independent evidence.

Tender pricing, concentrated buyers, customer backward integration, defects, raw-material inflation, energy costs and low initial yields can weaken returns. Operating EBITDA margins fell from 36.05% in FY2024 to 31.14% in FY2026, contrary to an unstoppable pricing-power thesis. MOAT 6 recognizes a useful but contestable qualification and process advantage.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Consolidated revenue progressed from ₹4.5885 crore in FY2022 to ₹16.2307 crore in FY2023, ₹47.3342 crore in FY2024, ₹70.5912 crore in FY2025 and ₹98.3469 crore in FY2026. Annual additions were ₹11.6422, ₹31.1035, ₹23.2570 and ₹27.7557 crore. The historical table retains every year. FY2021 previous-GAAP revenue was ₹1.8439 crore, but this was a trading business. Its high five-year reported CAGR and the FY2023–26 three-year CAGR are not comparable organic manufacturing rates.

The scoring basis was selected before assigning REV: manufacturing-led standalone FY2024–26 sales rose from ₹47.2274 crore to ₹98.2373 crore, a 44.23% two-year CAGR, with ₹70.1989 crore in FY2025. No material acquisition explains the expansion. A sufficient price-versus-volume bridge is not disclosed, so this is sales growth rather than verified tonnage growth. The preferred five- and three-year organic manufacturing windows cannot be established across the business-model transition. REV starts at 9 for growth above 30%, then is capped at 8 for short comparable history and Medium confidence. There is no second small-base penalty.

FY2026 second-half revenue of ₹54.20 crore versus ₹35.38 crore grew about 53.2%. The first-half amounts derived from annual totals were about ₹44.15 crore versus ₹35.21 crore, approximately 25.4% growth. This supports expansion across both halves, not only one exceptional quarter. Capacity and order-book claims belong in forward runway, not historical REV.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The accessible growth path is to deepen approved products at the existing 8,087-tonne plant, ramp the additional 13,200-tonne facility, and sell higher-value bogie, coupler and coach components. Dated purchase orders establish customer access. India's total railway budget is not the company's revenue opportunity. Management order-book snapshots around ₹140–160 crore lack an opening-plus-intake-minus-execution-and-cancellations reconciliation and must not be added again to individual orders.

The base experiment assumes existing-line utilization rising from 80% to 87%, new effective annual utilization from 10% to 72%, and initial realization of ₹1.8 lakh per tonne growing 3%. Base FY2027 revenue is ₹140.21 crore. This is below the preferential valuer's ₹266.84 crore FY2027 projection. That valuation also assumed no capex throughout its forecast and no debt despite audited borrowings, so its result is not adopted. Our model retains maintenance capex of 2.5% of sales plus ₹4–6 crore annual expansion after the IPO project.

Capital returns are mixed. FY2024–25 incremental NOPAT/IC was 22.11%, FY2025–26 was 8.23%, and the combined two-year figure was 11.42%. This is below the reasoned 12–16% industrial capital-cost range, but ₹38.16 crore of CWIP and ₹4.81 crore of capital advances were not yet generating mature returns. CAP 5 therefore does not extrapolate either the old plant's success or the new cohort's early low return. The runway requires collection, yield and approval progress, not merely installed equipment.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The promoter family held 70.03% of shares at March 2026, and the Managing Director also serves as CFO. Related flows include ₹1.2 crore promoter remuneration, ₹0.36 crore rent and facility charges, ₹0.25 crore related hiring charges, advances and promoter-linked foundation CSR. These are disclosed relationships, not automatic evidence of abuse. Arm's-length assertions should be tested against contracts and commercial alternatives. Gold of ₹2.9229 crore and an intercorporate deposit of ₹3.8315 crore also warrant capital-allocation scrutiny during a manufacturing expansion.

Execution has positives: trading became machining and manufacturing, capacity expanded to 8,087 tonnes, revenue roughly doubled over FY2024–26 and dated orders broadened access. The new project moved from earlier Kanpur plans to Haridwar. Earlier June 2026 timing changed to scheduled commercial production on 13 September 2026. The 7/8 August filings use commencement language in their headings but future scheduling in their bodies. Actual monthly qualified output, yields and cost to complete are not independently established at cutoff. The October explanation of delayed AGM proceedings is a modest disclosure-control lapse, not evidence of fraud.

FY2026 main audit and IFC opinions are unmodified. CARO reports matching bank returns and no default or fraud. Nevertheless, the audit trail could technically be disabled, although it operated and was preserved with no observed tampering. TDS, advance-tax, PF and ESI delays were noted, with no undisputed dues outstanding over six months. FY2023's unmodified report included capital/allotment compliance, sampled cash-labour verification and management balance-confirmation observations. The prospectus reports no quantifiable audit qualification but does not expressly close every old observation.

The original FY2022 audit repeats the same five observations later found in FY2023, despite retaining some stale FY2021 boilerplate dates. These are historical control limitations, not a formal qualified opinion.

FY2025 CARO also reported quarterly bank-return mismatches, including March raw-material and semi-finished differences of ₹264.47 lakh and ₹108.79 lakh. Management attributed these to inventory valuation/finalization timing and post-submission receipts. The note headings appear reversed against the auditor table, so the original labelled rows are preserved separately. FY2026 CARO reports agreement, which is meaningful later counterevidence but not a line-by-line closure of every old discrepancy.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY2026 PBT of ₹30.1613 crore plus finance cost of ₹1.5467 crore less other income of ₹3.2443 crore gives operating EBIT of ₹28.4637 crore. Adding ₹2.1629 crore depreciation gives operating EBITDA of ₹30.6266 crore. Other income includes ₹1.3066 crore unrealized gold gain and ₹1.9374 crore interest. The primary-supported tax rate is 17.16%; 25.17% is a stress. Reported EPS of ₹6.91 uses weighted shares, while owner PAT divided by current issued shares is ₹6.4457.

The analytical FY2026 cash bridge starts with reported CFO of ₹4.0277 crore. Removing release of ₹1.6205 crore prior-year prepaid IPO costs gives ₹2.4072 crore. Reclassifying ₹3.8315 crore ICD outflow to investing gives ₹6.2387 crore. Removing ₹0.9926 crore capital-creditor financing from operating cash gives ₹5.2461 crore. Offsetting changes elsewhere preserve net cash. Corresponding economic cash capex is ₹52.1637 crore versus reported ₹53.1563 crore. Three-year reported CFO/PAT is 44.80%, or 47.05% after these explicit adjustments. This remains weak, even though growth capex is not maintenance expense.

FY2025 original CFO of ₹12.2786 crore versus comparative ₹12.5092 crore reconciles: finance-cost addback increases ₹0.4036 crore and other financial assets decrease ₹0.1730 crore; other WC/tax changes net to zero. CFI and CFF offset the difference. Gold of ₹1.6163 crore was reclassified into reported capex, leaving industrial capex around ₹14.8110 crore. These are not missing-cash claims. In contrast, IPO costs of ₹8.0491 crore in note 45 versus ₹9.4163 crore charged to equity leave ₹1.3672 crore unexplained. Manufacturing utilization falls from ₹39.4665 crore in March to ₹36.46 crore in the June declaration, an unexplained ₹3.0065 crore decrease.

Net receivables rose to ₹31.8819 crore from ₹10.42 crore, and closing receivable days rose from 53.88 to 118.32. Most gross balances are less than six months overdue; ₹2.3964 crore are six to twelve months overdue and ₹0.0661 crore one to two years. None is presumed wholly uncollectible. Smaller face/note differences in payables and customer advances are separately tracked. The capital bridge retains CWIP and advances while removing non-operating financial assets; it is an invested-capital proxy, not a mature-project IRR.

Original FY2022 statutory PAT was ₹9.65060 lakh versus ₹7.03 lakh in the later prospectus restated/special-purpose basis, with essentially unchanged PBT of ₹12.87 lakh. Original revenue ₹462.96274 lakh and other income ₹0.02456 lakh largely reclassify into ₹458.85 lakh and ₹4.13 lakh. Cash remains ₹5.22 lakh within rounding, while total assets differ. The PAT difference is arithmetically explained by later tax categories: current tax ₹3.60 lakh, deferred tax ₹1.45 lakh and prior-year tax ₹0.79 lakh, totaling ₹5.84 lakh versus original ₹3.21687 lakh, with a ₹0.00253 lakh PBT rounding difference. The rationale and complete original-to-special-purpose balance bridge are not established. This is separate from the prospectus IndAS transition reconciliation, which starts from the later previous-GAAP basis. Latest restated figures are used consistently; no missing current cash is inferred.

The ₹3.0065 crore current IPO utilization discrepancy is about 75% of FY2026 reported CFO and 27% of stated unspent IPO funds. Its materiality to available liquidity, rather than the ordinary prior-year cash classifications, supports the bounded G2 Hold.

Normalized return on average invested-capital proxy is about 41.22% in FY2025 and 26.85% in FY2026. These high blended returns reflect the successful legacy asset base and do not replace the lower incremental-return test for the recent deployment. Reported ROE on average book equity falls from approximately 51.03% to 27.48% as IPO capital enters.

The original FY2023 pack is also distinct: revenue ₹1,651.53 lakh, other income ₹3.34 lakh, PBT/PAT ₹57.19 lakh and assets ₹1,349.71 lakh, versus prospectus restated ₹1,623.07 lakh, ₹9.76 lakh, ₹56.27/₹42.32 lakh and ₹1,463.14 lakh. Its FY2022 comparative PAT is ₹12.18 lakh, different again from the original FY2022 pack. The later special-purpose baseline is not the original statutory baseline. A complete bridge is unavailable, so original history is not described as fully reconciled; this does not change the selected FY2024–26 growth or current cash model.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹233.40, market capitalization is ₹905.89 crore and current-share P/E is 36.21 times. Operating EV before unverified cash offsets is ₹909.85 crore, including ₹3.878 crore debt and ₹0.0865 crore minority interest, or about 29.71 times operating EBITDA. IPO funds, long-tenor deposits, gold, ICD and receivables are not all free cash. Operating property is not added a second time to earnings-based EV. Current peer multiples are not imported without verified comparable prices and business scope.

The cash model starts on 31 March 2026 and bridges through entry to 20 October 2031. Even assuming redeemability of ₹10 crore other-bank deposits, cash of ₹11.8571 crore less stated IPO earmarks of ₹11.3184 crore leaves only ₹0.5387 crore before an analyst reserve of ₹3 crore. The opening ₹2.4613 crore reserve gap is pre-entry, not an observed default. Reserves scale with revenue; each interval's uses are prefunded before operating receipts. Remaining project spend of ₹11.3172 crore includes existing capital creditors and commitments, while capital advances were already paid. Old tax, expense dues and gratuity are paid once, separate from future taxes.

The issuer-signed 27 August allotment document, recovered through a secondary mirror, reports receipt of ₹6.87024 crore upfront for warrants. Its remaining ₹20.61072 crore is optional, not present cash. The model distinguishes both flows and adds conversion shares only with conversion money. Current available balances still require the IPO roll-forward. All ordinary IRRs, non-rescue conditional IRRs and entry prices remain NS.

Counterfactual rescue issues whole shares at ₹163.38 with 3% fees before each gap, including hypothetical pre-entry injections. Under that artificial funded history, bear/base/bull IRRs are -17.71%, 10.79% and 22.74%, using trailing-365-day terminal EBITDA at 8/14/18 times. Base rescue needs ₹5.55 crore net. Its 15%-hurdle price of ₹193.70 is not a buying range. Base terminal LTM revenue is ₹335.40 crore, EBITDA ₹93.91 crore and retained operating cash ₹10.53 crore. The 15% reverse root requires about ₹405.76 crore LTM revenue but pushes the old line above 100% utilization under proportional scaling. The 18% root also exceeds total capacity. Finite mathematical roots therefore do not establish physical or investment feasibility. Complete joint sensitivities and dated cash rows follow.

There is a published financing alternative: FY2025 notes disclose an ₹8 crore Central Bank working-capital sanction. Compared with the FY2026 ₹3.862 crore revolver, potential headroom is ₹4.138 crore if the limit and drawing power continue. FY2026 confirms bank working-capital facilities, but current renewal, drawing power and unrestricted availability are not verified. Additional dated counterfactual cases draw this headroom at opening, charge 8.6% interest and repay both incremental and existing revolver on 31 March 2027. These test ₹1.5 crore and ₹3 crore reserves with and without equity rescue. They prevent the false implication that all financing gaps inevitably require equity; they do not establish an actual historical draw or cure the IPO reconciliation. In the base case, the lower ₹1.5 crore reserve is mathematically maintained using only the hypothetical bank bridge, giving a funding-only diagnostic IRR of 10.93%; at the ₹3 crore reserve, ₹1.44 crore additional net equity is needed. This is meaningful financing counterevidence, but neither branch establishes current available liquidity or an ordinary investment return.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not that railway demand disappears. It is that orders arrive but customers retain the cash while investors pay today for an efficiently ramped future factory. Delayed qualification and low yields raise unit costs; material costs or rejections compress margins; receivables extend; and growth capex persists. The business may remain profitable while minority investors lose through dilution, financing costs and multiple compression.

The funded counterfactual bear ends near ₹88.07 per share versus ₹233.40, roughly 62% capital impairment over five years despite positive operating earnings. Without its hypothetical rescue, cash-floor breaches invalidate an ordinary return figure. Modest debt, repayment of term loans and clean bank-return audit findings are important counterweights. The analyst's reserve is neither a disclosed bank covenant nor evidence of an actual missed payment.

Permanent-loss risk rises if aged receivables grow over successive periods, adjusted CFO/PAT stays below 0.6, new capital fails to earn its cost after stabilization, or the IPO ledger cannot be reconciled. Evidence of diversion, undisclosed guarantees, default or an adverse auditor change would require immediate G1/G2 reassessment. None is assumed proven here.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold share price in five years requires approximately 38% annual appreciation; tenfold requires approximately 58.5%, before transaction costs. The embedded calculation holds base counterfactual cash, dilution and a 14-times terminal multiple constant to derive required EBITDA and revenue at a 28% margin. It is a constraint test, not a forecast or a probability estimate.

The base FY2032 full-year capacity plan produces ₹345.13 crore revenue and already requires substantial ramp-up. The fivefold test requires revenue well above ₹1,000 crore, while tenfold is more demanding still. Such outcomes would need additional physical capacity, materially richer mix or pricing, working capital and further funding. Those requirements are absent when base cash and dilution are held constant, so the test cannot support a financed multibagger thesis. Current company size, railway budgets and promotional EPS growth are insufficient substitutes for this operating and financing bridge.

Numerically, fivefold requires about ₹311.39 crore terminal EBITDA and ₹1,112.10 crore revenue; tenfold requires ₹637.84 crore EBITDA and ₹2,277.99 crore revenue under those deliberately fixed assumptions. These requirements are far above the base LTM EBITDA of ₹93.91 crore.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Monitor operating evidence, not only the quote. The KPI register below gives baselines, required observations and warning thresholds. The first priorities are the signed IPO/available-cash reconciliation, actual qualified output from the new plant and customer collections. Revenue growth without improved realization does not remove the GQS cash ceiling. A declaration of no deviation is not enough if its numerical utilization roll-forward conflicts with audited notes.

The most useful next public documents are September 2026 half-year results and cash flow, the monitoring agency's object-wise IPO report, actual commissioning and dispatch disclosures, and primary warrant conversion records. Collection improvement should be checked for factoring or other financing reclassification. After a full ramp, incremental returns should clear the 12–16% capital-cost range. Until then, scenario assumptions remain explicit rather than management-certified forecasts. No external recurring monitoring service has been created.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: a mixed-quality, expansion-led industrial growth candidate. It is not a qualified compounder and is not currently an actionable investment recommendation. BQS 5.3 is provisional and excluded from quality rankings; GQS 5.0 is cash-capped and also excluded while G2 remains Hold. IAS is NS, not zero and not an estimated midpoint.

Action: research Hold. Reconcile IPO costs, utilization and available cash; verify actual qualified capacity ramp; retain issuer-reported warrant receipts separately from remaining optional consideration; then rebuild returns and test a full 60-session exit window for the intended position. Only after these conditions are met should an actionable 15%-hurdle entry range be considered. The counterfactual ₹193.70 base hurdle price is not that range because it assumes historical capital injections and specific operating outcomes.

The case improves if collections normalize without financing being presented as operating cash, the new plant stays within its remaining budget and mature incremental returns exceed the capital cost. It worsens with unexplained fund use, growing aged receivables, recurring non-operating financial placements or unfinanced overruns. These are observable conditions, not promises of investment returns.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary sources include complete FY2026 and FY2025 annual reports, earlier financial packs, the July 2025 prospectus, dated order and plant filings, the IPO deviation statement and warrant terms. Main audit, CARO, IFC and audit-trail annexures were inspected. The prospectus IndAS transition adjustments are modest, but its preceding special-purpose restatements also contain policy, error and regrouping adjustments; original FY2025 cash-flow classifications are preserved alongside the comparative presentation. SHA256 hashes identify inspected documents. The issuer-signed warrant allotment document was recovered through a secondary mirror; this improves documentary evidence but does not authenticate the original exchange download or independently verify the bank balance.

Material open questions are the IPO expense and utilization roll-forward; deposit availability, encumbrances and current earmarked cash; actual plant tonnage, yield and remaining cost; customer acceptance and collection terms; smaller face/note payable differences; and current exchange restrictions and a 60-session liquidity window. Missing FY2021 CFO is NS, not zero. The dated secondary close is a research reference, not a guaranteed executable bid.

Analyst assumptions are separately identified: utilization, realization, margins, receivable/inventory/payable days, government-credit buildup, maintenance and growth capex, scaled reserves, optional conversion timing, taxes, terminal multiples and rescue terms. Full annual, interval and sensitivity rows permit reconstruction without raw copyrighted PDFs or personal annexures. Counterfactual rescue illustrates economics but cannot establish historical funding. An unreconciled table is not, by itself, an allegation of misuse or fraud.

evidence.claim: FY2026 consolidated revenue was ₹98.3469 crore, PAT ₹25.0134 crore, owner PAT ₹25.0174 crore and reported CFO ₹4.0277 crore. Revenue rose 39.32%; CFO/PAT was 16.10%.
FY2026 operating EBITDA of ₹30.6266 crore excludes other income of ₹3.2443 crore, including interest of ₹1.9374 crore and an unrealized gold gain of ₹1.3066 crore.
FY2024–26 reported CFO of ₹24.2095 crore divided by PAT of ₹54.0436 crore is 44.80%. Explicit FY2026 prepaid-IPO, ICD and capital-creditor reclasses raise this to 47.05%, still weak.

Net receivables were ₹31.8819 crore versus ₹10.42 crore; closing days rose from 53.88 to 118.32. Gross balances include ₹2.3964 crore six-to-twelve months overdue and ₹0.0661 crore one-to-two years overdue; ECL is ₹0.3216 crore.
Three customers each exceeding 10% contributed 52.35% of FY2026 sales; the largest contributed 28.90%. FY2024 top-ten concentration was 94.36%, a different denominator.

Existing capacity of 8,087 tonnes plus the new 13,200-tonne plan implies 21,287 tonnes. More than 25 approved safety components support qualification access; scheduled September 2026 commissioning does not establish actual tonnage.
evidence.locator: S01 business; S04 dated8Aug body explicitly scheduled

evidence.claim: Manufacturing-led standalone sales grew from ₹47.2274 crore in FY2024 to ₹98.2373 crore in FY2026, a 44.23% CAGR. The earlier trading transition makes longer reported growth non-comparable.
Operating EBITDA margins declined from 36.05% in FY2024 to 32.89% in FY2025 and 31.14% in FY2026, despite growing operating profit.
Incremental NOPAT/IC was 22.11% for FY2024–25, 8.23% for FY2025–26 and 11.42% combined. FY2026 capital includes ₹38.1621 crore CWIP and ₹4.8097 crore capital advances awaiting mature returns.
IPO expenses of ₹8.0491 crore in note 45 differ from the ₹9.4163 crore equity charge by ₹1.3672 crore. Net issue cash of ₹67.6236 crore aligns with the larger deduction from gross ₹77.04 crore.

March manufacturing IPO utilization of ₹39.4665 crore falls to ₹36.46 crore in the June declaration, an unexplained ₹3.0065 crore decrease. Other objects appear cumulative; this is not proof of diversion.

Cash of ₹1.8571 crore plus ₹10 crore other-bank deposits less stated IPO earmarks of ₹11.3184 crore leaves ₹0.5387 crore, even assuming deposit availability. Gold, ICD and other receivables are not assured free cash.

Debt of ₹3.878 crore includes a ₹3.862 crore revolver at 8.6% and ₹0.016 crore director loan. Capital commitments are ₹4.8052 crore, capital creditors ₹0.9926 crore and current tax payable ₹3.1558 crore.

FY2026 audit and IFC opinions are unmodified, bank returns agree and no default or fraud is reported. Audit-trail disablement is technically possible; no tampering was observed. Some statutory-payment delays occurred, none undisputed beyond six months. FY2025 bank-return mismatches and management timing explanations are retained separately; FY2026 agreement is later counterevidence, not proof that earlier quarters always matched.

FY2023 audit was unmodified but included capital/allotment compliance, sampled cash-labour work and management balance-confirmation observations. The prospectus found no quantifiable audit qualifications; modest IndAS adjustments do not constitute missing cash. The FY2022 original audit repeats these observations; original statutory PAT differs from the later special-purpose baseline, a separate historical reconciliation gap. FY2023 original PBT/PAT and assets also differ from the later special-purpose basis; a complete bridge is unavailable.

FY2025 original CFO of ₹12.2786 crore versus comparative ₹12.5092 crore reconciles by classification, offset in investing and financing. Net cash is unchanged within rounding; ₹1.6163 crore gold moved into reported capex.

Promoters held 70.03% at March 2026. Related flows include ₹1.2 crore promoter remuneration, ₹0.36 crore rent/facility charges, ₹0.25 crore related hiring charges and ₹0.2384 crore CSR. The MD also serves as CFO.
evidence.locator: Governance shareholding and note35; flows not all expense

evidence.claim: The issuer-signed 27 August 2026 allotment filing, recovered through a secondary mirror, reports 2,642,400 warrants at ₹104 and 25% upfront receipt of ₹6.87024 crore. The remaining ₹20.61072 crore is optional; full conversion adds 6.81% shares.
evidence.locator: S57 PDF pages 1 and 5, issuer-signed original; later revised relay retained.

evidence.claim: May 2026 orders of ₹14.76 crore and July orders of ₹17.12 crore demonstrate access. Management order-book snapshots around ₹140–160 crore are not reconciled revenue or cash and must not be double-counted.

Qualification and inspection reduce substitutability, but Texmaco, HEIL, Steelcast and Braithwaite provide structural alternatives. Verified item-level market share or sole-source privilege is unavailable.

The dated 19 October 2026 reference close is ₹233.40, implying ₹905.8861 crore market capitalization and 36.21 times FY2026 owner PAT on current issued shares. Weighted EPS of ₹6.91 is not current-share EPS of ₹6.4457.

Twenty dated secondary sessions imply mean turnover ₹2.0804432 crore and median ₹2.003948 crore. Missing 60-session history is not zero volume. Three 800-share lots cost ₹560,160, above the ₹500,000 reference position.

The counterfactual cash model exposes pre-entry reserve gaps, separates IPO earmarks and optional warrant money, includes old taxes and dues, funds ongoing capex and retains terminal reserves. All ordinary returns remain NS.
Joint sensitivities test collections, capex, margin, multiple, tax, deposits and optional conversion. Reverse roots require finite sign-crossing and separate line-level physical-capacity tests.
FY2021 audited previous-GAAP trading revenue was ₹1.8439125 crore and PAT ₹0.0855985 crore. This is not a comparable organic manufacturing base; FY2021 CFO remains unverified.

valuation_and_funding_model.timing_policy: Monthly plus entry, receipt and conversion dates. summary:
Neetu Yoshi is a railway-component casting and machining manufacturer expanding into larger assemblies. It is an industrial growth candidate, not yet a demonstrated compounder. Safety-item qualifications, repeat orders and rapidly growing sales are its strengths. Cash realization and the reconciliation of IPO-funded expansion are its principal weaknesses. FY2026 revenue rose 39.32% to ₹98.35 crore, but reported operating cash was only ₹4.03 crore against ₹25.01 crore PAT.

At the dated secondary-market reference of ₹233.40 on 19 October 2026, market capitalization is ₹905.89 crore. That is 36.21 times FY2026 profit using current issued shares and about 29.71 times operating EBITDA before unverified cash deductions. The price therefore requires substantial successful growth. Provisional BQS is 5.3/10; GQS is 5.0/10 after its persistent-cash ceiling; IAS is NS. Quality and growth diagnostics are excluded from rankings while G2 is on Hold.

Research verdict: Hold. The current IPO ledger contains material unresolved differences, although the audited cash-flow reclassifications themselves reconcile. Ordinary investment returns and an actionable buying range are not supported. A signed IPO and available-cash reconciliation, verified new-plant dispatches, and sustained collections would improve the case. A lower quote alone would not cure the funding evidence gap.
